a parser trained jointly on syntactic and semantic information produces syntactic parses and logical forms that are better than those produced by parsers trained separately on the same information.

a parser that jointly learns syntax and semantics produces better semantic representations than a parser that learns only semantics or a pipelined parser that learns only syntax then semantics and that this joint learning parser produces better syntax than a parser that is trained only on syntax.
a parser can be trained to simultaneously produce syntactic parses and logical forms for portions with a semantic representation within a given predicate vocabulary.

the problem of joint syntactic and semantics parsing, which is an important component of the broader problem of semantic parsing.
the problem of training a single parser that can produce both syntactic parses and logical forms for a large vocabulary of predicates.
the problem of jointly learning a syntactic and semantic analysis of natural language sentences.
